root_cause_short: SwapNet Router's swap function (0x87395540) performed a low-level call to a user-supplied target with user-controlled calldata; attacker set target to USDC and calldata to transferFrom to drain approvals.
exploit_steps: Identified closed-source SwapNet Router on Base at 0x616000e384Ef1C2B52f5f3A88D57a3B64F23757e
Crafted malicious swap parameters setting call target to the USDC contract
Crafted calldata invoking USDC.transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount)
Router's low-level call executed attacker-controlled transferFrom against approved balances
Drained ~$13.34M USDC from single largest victim; 20 users total across Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BSC
Swapped ~$10.5M USDC to ~3,655 ETH on Base
Bridged stolen funds to Ethereum mainnet
SwapNet paused contracts ~45 minutes after initial exploit
invariant_broken: Aggregator low-level calls must validate target address against a whitelist of known DEX routers; arbitrary user-supplied targets must be rejected.
prerequisites: Closed-source aggregator with permissionless external call
Users with infinite token approvals to router
mitigation_class: Strict Call-Target Whitelist + Function-Selector Validation + Per-Tx Approval Patterns
notes: Closed-source contracts complicated analysis; decompiled bytecode revealed vulnerable function 0x87395540(). Affected Matcha Meta users who disabled default One-Time Approval. Same-day attacker cluster with Aperture Finance; AMLBot clustering also links to Li.Fi/Jumper Exchange 2024 exploits.
reconciliation_notes: Grok v1 reported $16M (conflated with Aperture's $3.67M). Reconciled to $13.4M for SwapNet-only per The Block, Verichains, ExVul, Cryptopolitan. Chain corrected from 'base' to 'multi' with chain_primary=base.

root_cause_short: Function 0x67b34120 invoked internal 0x1d33 executing low-level calls with user-supplied calldata without enforcing strict target/selector constraints; enabled ERC-20 drainage and Uniswap V3 NFT approvals.
exploit_steps: Invoked Aperture function 0x67b34120 with crafted payload
Internal 0x1d33 executed user-controlled low-level call
Malicious calldata triggered ERC-20 transferFrom against approvals
Same path approved Uniswap V3 position NFTs to attacker
$3.67M drained across chains
invariant_broken: Aggregator low-level calls must validate target address and function selector; NFT approvals must not be reachable via arbitrary calldata paths.
prerequisites: Users with active approvals (including NFT) to Aperture
mitigation_class: Call-Target + Selector Whitelist; Periodic NFT Approval Revocation
notes: Same day as SwapNet, same attacker cluster per AMLBot clustering. Aperture acknowledged vulnerability and opened on-chain communication with perpetrator. Attacker hub address 0x6cAad74121bF602e71386505A4687f310e0D833e links this cluster to Li.Fi / Jumper Exchange 2024 exploits.
reconciliation_notes: Record was missing from both Grok runs; reconstructed from search results during SwapNet reconciliation pass. Demonstrates the Grok prompt's cluster-inclusion failure that v2 must fix.

root_cause_short: Months-long social engineering induced 2-of-5 Security Council signers to pre-sign durable-nonce transactions; zero-timelock governance permitted instant admin takeover; fake CVT collateral at manipulated oracle price then drained real assets.
exploit_steps: Attacker conducted multi-month social engineering posing as a quantitative trading firm
Mar 11 2026: on-chain staging begins with 10 ETH withdrawal from Tornado Cash
Mar 12 2026: deployed CVT (CarbonVote Token) as fake collateral; wash-traded to anchor ~$1 on small Raydium pool; set attacker-controlled oracle
Mar 23-30: created durable nonce accounts bound to Security Council signer keys
Tricked signers into approving pre-authorization transactions believing them routine
Apr 1 ~16:05 UTC: triggered the pre-signed txs, transferring admin control to attacker address with zero timelock
Whitelisted CVT as collateral with infinite borrowing limits and manipulated oracle price
Deposited 500M CVT and executed 31 rapid withdrawals totaling $285M over ~12 minutes
Swapped assets via Jupiter, bridged via CCTP to Ethereum, converted to ETH
invariant_broken: Governance/admin actions must require fresh, timelocked multisig approvals; no indefinitely-valid pre-signed authorizations should be possible on critical paths.
prerequisites: Multisig with zero timelock on Security Council migration
Durable nonce feature usable for critical governance txs
Social engineering access to threshold signers
mitigation_class: Mandatory Timelocks on Governance + Signer Environment Isolation (EDR) + Durable Nonce Restriction for Privileged Paths + Independent Signer Device Payload Decoding
notes: Largest DeFi hack of 2026; second-largest Solana exploit in history behind only the 2022 Wormhole bridge hack. Drift was audited by Trail of Bits (2022) and ClawSecure (Feb 2026); governance weaknesses fell outside code-scoped audits. SEAL 911 attributed same threat actor as Radiant Capital Oct 2024 (UNC4736 / AppleJeus / Citrine Sleet). Circle criticized on X for delayed USDC freeze during 6-hour CCTP bridge window.
